plan.headline: Wave 1 is posted for the fight at Sat 10/17 8:10 PM CT. 420 sold, 1,980 resting; 1,500 more post at Sat 10/17 9:00 AM CT. Worst line -$370.
plan.confidence_note: Every step below is a timer or rule in the bot's settings, and the bot is healthy. The fight start time is an estimate and can move.

sections.title: Right now
lines: Wave 1 (lowest rung only). Fight start estimate Sat 10/17 8:10 PM CT (in 2d 21h).
Moneyline right now: Barriault 36% to win, Daukaus 64%.
Sold 420 contracts so far; 1,980 more resting across 6 buckets. Premium $50.
Worst line -$370 (-$6 if every resting order filled). Backstop -$250; trickle target -$100 by the fight.
Wave 1 holds back 1,500 contracts of the ladder (only the lowest rung is posted) until Sat 10/17 9:00 AM CT (in 2d 9h).
Backstop is ON for Daukaus by Submission: its line is under -$250, so nothing more is added there until the others catch up.
Bot is healthy: heartbeat 4s old, no errors.

sections.title: Lagging sides
lines: Barriault by KO/TKO: sold 0, 420 behind the leader. Cheapest row 16c, fair 15.1c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 13.1c (fair minus 2c, or the crowd's clearing price if higher), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. 280 more contracts are held back for the full-ladder release.

Barriault by Submission: sold 0, 420 behind the leader. Cheapest row 7c, fair 5.9c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 3.9c (fair minus 2c, or the crowd's clearing price if higher), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. 100 more contracts are held back for the full-ladder release.

Barriault by Decision: sold 0, 420 behind the leader. Cheapest row 15c, fair 14.2c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 12.2c (fair minus 2c, or the crowd's clearing price if higher), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. 280 more contracts are held back for the full-ladder release.

Daukaus by KO/TKO: sold 0, 420 behind the leader. Cheapest row 30c, fair 27.4c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 25.4c (fair minus 2c, or the crowd's clearing price if higher), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. 280 more contracts are held back for the full-ladder release.

Daukaus by Decision: sold 0, 420 behind the leader. Cheapest row 28c, fair 25.7c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 23.7c (fair minus 2c, or the crowd's clearing price if higher), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. 280 more contracts are held back for the full-ladder release.
The bot checks every 45s. The moneyline is rechecked every 5m (every 1m in the last 3 hours). Rows already resting are not repriced when the line moves; only new rows use the fresh fair.
A step is skipped if filling the new row in full would push the worst line lower.

sections.title: Next wave of contracts
lines: Wave 1 is posted: one lowest rung per bucket. At Sat 10/17 9:00 AM CT (in 2d 9h) the bot releases the rest of every ladder: 1,500 more contracts across 6 buckets.
Extra batches: a bucket whose resting falls under 25% of its allotment gets a batch of 50% of it (a third inside T-30), split 60/25/15 across three prices, up to 3 batches, 20 min apart, until T-3.
Daukaus by Submission is thin (0 resting) but is 420 contracts ahead of the least-sold bucket (limit 300), so it gets no batch until the others catch up.
Closest to triggering: Barriault by KO/TKO with 420 resting against a trigger of 105.
The worst-line gate is closed: batches wait until the worst line is -$100 or better (it is -$370).
Batches used so far: none.

sections.title: Tightening
lines: Trickle balancing starts at T-120 (Sat 10/17 6:10 PM CT, in 2d 19h): the bot records the worst line then and walks it to -$100 by the fight, selling small clips (50 contracts) at the bid, checking every 5 min, paying only when more than $25 behind, at most $100 paid per book.

From T-30: queue-preserving even-up (a bucket 15% behind the leader gets its lowest rung moved toward fair without losing queue). From T-5: a last-resort take is allowed; it is the old one-shot balancer and spends at most half the banked margin.
Between T-120 and T-30 the evenness allowance tightens on a time schedule, because a fight can end in seconds.
The fight start is an estimate from the card position on ESPN; if earlier bouts run long it moves, and every T- time here moves with it.

sections.title: Will it adapt on its own?
lines: Yes, on its own: the full ladder at the release time, extra batches on thin buckets while the gate is open, price steps on lagging buckets, and the paid trickle from T-120.
No, it will not: reprice resting rows when the moneyline moves, or add anything once the worst line is under the gate. The start time can shift if earlier bouts run long.
Depends on the crowd: the worst line is -$370 against a -$100 target. The trickle covers up to $100; the rest depends on fills on the lagging buckets.
I only read the bot's settings, state and log. I cannot see its next decision, only the rules it follows.
